templates.name: Consultancy
templates.summary: Three pages for advisers, agencies and independent professionals: what you do, how you work, and a way to reach you.

pages.title: Home
pages.seo_description: Independent advice for owner-led companies: strategy reviews, operations and interim leadership.

sections.heading: Advice that survives contact with your business
sections.subheading: We work with owner-led companies on the decisions that are too big to guess at.

items.title: Strategy reviews
items.body: A short, structured look at where the business makes money and where it leaks it, ending in a written plan you own.

items.title: Operations
items.body: Process, tooling and reporting for teams that have outgrown the spreadsheet they started on.

items.title: Interim leadership
items.body: Hands-on cover for a role you are recruiting for, so the work does not stop while you hire.

sections.heading: Start with a conversation
sections.body: Thirty minutes, no charge, and an honest answer about whether we are the right people for the work.

sections.heading: How we work
sections.subheading: Short engagements, written conclusions, and no dependency on us afterwards.

items.title: 1. A conversation
items.body: We listen to the problem as you describe it and say plainly whether it is one we can help with.

items.title: 2. A written proposal
items.body: Scope, price and the date you get the work back, on one page, before anything starts.

items.title: 3. The work
items.body: We do it, we write it down, and we hand it over so your team can keep running it without us.

items.question: How long does an engagement take?
items.answer: Most reviews take two to four weeks. Anything longer is split into stages you can stop between.

items.question: Do you work with our existing team?
items.answer: Always. Nothing we recommend works if the people who run it every day were not part of deciding it.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: Replace this answer with your own pricing, or say that you quote per engagement after the first call.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.subheading: Tell us what you are working on. We read every message ourselves.

sections.heading: Send a message
sections.body: Add your phone number and address here if you would rather be called.
sections.success_message: Thank you — your message has arrived and we will reply within one working day.

templates.name: Restaurant or café
templates.summary: A room, a menu and directions: the three pages a kitchen actually needs, with a booking enquiry form.

pages.title: Home
pages.seo_description: A neighbourhood kitchen with a short seasonal menu. See the menu, opening hours and how to find us.

sections.heading: A neighbourhood kitchen
sections.subheading: Seasonal cooking, a short menu that changes with the market, and a room worth staying in.

items.title: Lunch
items.body: A two-course plate cooked from whatever came in that morning, served quickly enough to get back to work.

items.title: Dinner
items.body: A longer menu, a small wine list chosen by the people who pour it, and no rush to turn the table.

items.title: Private hire
items.body: The room seats a group for a birthday, a wake or a company dinner. Write to us and we will plan it with you.

sections.heading: Come and eat
sections.body: Walk in, or write ahead if you are more than four.

sections.heading: The menu
sections.subheading: It changes with the season. Replace these dishes with yours and add your prices.

items.title: To start
items.body: Describe two or three small plates here — what is in them and where they came from.

items.title: Mains
items.body: Describe the plates the kitchen is proud of this week, with the price beside each one.

items.title: Puddings
items.body: One or two, written the way you would say them out loud at the table.

items.title: To drink
items.body: The wines, beers or coffees worth naming. A short list reads better than a long one.

items.question: Can you cook for dietary requirements?
items.answer: Say here what you can adapt and what you cannot, and ask guests to tell you when they book.

items.question: Are children welcome?
items.answer: Answer honestly — a family deciding where to eat would rather read it here than find out at the door.

sections.heading: Find us
sections.subheading: Add your address, the nearest stop and anything a first-time guest needs to know.

items.title: Lunch
items.body: Add the days and times you serve lunch, so nobody arrives to a closed door.

items.title: Dinner
items.body: Add the days and times you serve dinner, and the last order of the evening.

sections.heading: Book a table
sections.body: Tell us the date, the time and how many of you there are, and we will confirm by email.
sections.success_message: Thank you — we have your request and will confirm your table by email.

templates.name: Portfolio
templates.summary: For photographers, designers, studios and makers: the work first, a short note about you, and an enquiry form.

pages.title: Home
pages.seo_description: Selected work, how the studio works, and how to commission a project.

sections.heading: Work made carefully, for people who will use it
sections.subheading: Write one sentence here that a stranger could repeat to somebody else about what you make.

items.title: Commissions
items.body: Describe the kind of brief you do your best work on, and the size of project you take.

items.title: Collaborations
items.body: Say who you like working alongside — studios, agencies, other makers — and in what role.

items.title: Prints and licensing
items.body: If existing work can be bought or licensed, say so here and point at how.

sections.heading: Have something in mind?
sections.body: A paragraph about the project is enough to start. There is no form to fill in twice.

sections.heading: Selected work
sections.subheading: Replace these with your own projects, and add a picture to each one from the editor.

items.title: Project one
items.body: What it was, who it was for, and the one decision that made it work. Two sentences beat two paragraphs.

items.title: Project two
items.body: What the client needed, what you made, and what happened afterwards.

items.title: Project three
items.body: A piece you would take on again. Say why.

sections.heading: The full portfolio
sections.body: Add a gallery section here from the editor to show the pictures at full width.

sections.heading: Start a project
sections.subheading: Tell me what it is, roughly when it needs to exist, and I will tell you honestly if I am the right person.

sections.heading: Tell me about it
sections.success_message: Thank you — your note has arrived and you will hear back from me shortly.

templates.name: Association or charity
templates.summary: For clubs, associations and charities: the cause, the work it pays for, and the ways somebody can help.

pages.title: Home
pages.seo_description: What we do, who it helps, and how to take part or support the work.

sections.heading: Say the cause in one line, the way a member would say it
sections.subheading: Then say who it is for and where you work, so a stranger knows in five seconds whether this is their place.

items.title: What we run
items.body: Describe the activity somebody could turn up to next week, and where and when it happens.

items.title: Who it is for
items.body: Say plainly who is welcome and what it costs, if anything, to take part.

items.title: Who runs it
items.body: Volunteers, staff or both — say which, because people give differently when they know.

sections.heading: Take part
sections.body: Members, volunteers and donors all start the same way: by getting in touch.

sections.heading: What we do
sections.subheading: One paragraph on the problem, and one on what your organisation actually does about it.

items.title: Programme one
items.body: What happens, how often, and what it changes for the people it is for.

items.title: Programme two
items.body: The same, in the same length. Consistency reads as competence.

items.title: Programme three
items.body: If you only run two, delete this one rather than inventing a third.

items.question: Where does the money go?
items.answer: Answer with real figures once you have them, and link your annual accounts here.

items.question: How can I help if I have no money to give?
items.answer: Name the practical things — time, a skill, a room, a lift — that you genuinely need.

sections.heading: Get involved
sections.subheading: Join, volunteer, or ask a question. Somebody reads every message.

items.title: Become a member
items.body: Say what membership costs, what it gives, and how somebody joins.

items.title: Volunteer
items.body: Say what you need doing and how much time it takes. Vague asks get vague answers.

items.title: Donate
items.body: Add your bank details or donation link here once they are ready.

sections.heading: Write to us
sections.success_message: Thank you — your message has arrived and one of us will reply soon.

templates.name: Software or product
templates.summary: For a product or subscription: what it does, what it costs, and a way to ask. Prices are left blank for you to set.

pages.title: Home
pages.seo_description: What the product does, who it is for, and what it costs.

sections.heading: Say what it does, not what category it is in
sections.subheading: One sentence a customer could repeat to a colleague, and one on who it is for.

items.title: The first thing it does
items.body: Describe the job it does for the customer, in their words rather than yours.

items.title: The second thing
items.body: The next most common reason somebody buys it. Stop at three; a list of ten reads as none.

items.title: The third thing
items.body: Something true that a competitor cannot copy this quarter.

sections.heading: Try it with your own data
sections.body: Replace this with whatever the first real step is: a trial, a demo, or a conversation.

sections.heading: Pricing
sections.subheading: The prices below are blank on purpose — only you can set them.

sections.heading: Plans
sections.intro: Replace the names, the prices and the lines under them with your own.

tiers.name: Starter
features: Name the limit that defines this plan

tiers.name: Team
tiers.description: For a small team working together.
features: The thing teams actually pay more for

tiers.name: Company
tiers.description: For organisations with their own requirements.

items.question: Can I change plan later?
items.answer: Answer plainly, including what happens to money already paid.

items.question: Are the prices excluding VAT?
items.answer: Say which, every time. A price a business customer has to guess at is a price they distrust.

sections.heading: Ask us anything
sections.subheading: Questions about the product, the price or whether it fits how you already work.

sections.heading: Send a message
sections.success_message: Thank you — your message has arrived and we will reply within one working day.

templates.name: Local trade
templates.summary: For plumbers, electricians, builders and installers: the work you cover, the area you cover, and a quote request.

pages.title: Home
pages.seo_description: Local, insured and reachable: the work we cover, the area we cover, and how to get a quote.

sections.heading: The trade, the town, and a number that gets answered
sections.subheading: Put your trade and your area in this line — it is the only thing most visitors read.

items.title: We turn up
items.body: Say what somebody can expect: when you answer the phone, and how soon you can come out.

items.title: Fixed quotes
items.body: Say how you price the work and whether the quote can change once you have seen the job.

items.title: Insured and certified
items.body: List your certifications and registration numbers here — they are the reason a stranger trusts you.

sections.heading: Tell us about the job
sections.body: A sentence and a photo are usually enough for a first estimate.

sections.heading: What we do
sections.subheading: Keep this list to the work you want more of.

items.title: Repairs
items.body: The jobs you are called out to most. Say roughly how quickly you can get to one.

items.title: Installations
items.body: The planned work you quote for, and what a typical job involves from first visit to finish.

items.title: Maintenance
items.body: Anything you do on a contract or a yearly visit, and who it is worth having.

items.title: Emergencies
items.body: Say honestly whether you take emergency calls, when, and what that costs.

items.question: Which areas do you cover?
items.answer: Name the towns and postcodes. This is the question you are asked most often.

items.question: Do you charge for a quote?
items.answer: Answer plainly, including any call-out fee, so nobody is surprised on the doorstep.

sections.heading: Get a quote
sections.subheading: Describe the job and where you are. Add your phone number below if you would rather be called.

sections.heading: Tell us about the job
sections.body: The more you can say about the property and the problem, the closer the estimate will be.
sections.success_message: Thank you — we have the details and will come back to you with an estimate.
